key_insight: Polished cold-sprayed 316L coatings develop more noble, passive-like corrosion behavior than as-sprayed coatings or the SAE 1020 substrate, even with residual porosity.
engineering_relevance: Surface finishing is a critical post-process for making cold-sprayed stainless-steel coatings effective corrosion barriers on carbon steel in chloride environments.
method: Cold-sprayed 316L onto SAE 1020 at 650–825 °C gas temperature
Compared as-sprayed and polished surface conditions
Used OCP, EIS, and cyclic potentiodynamic polarization in 0.6 M NaCl
evidence_signal: Polished coatings showed more noble OCP, capacitive EIS responses, and sustained anodic polarization with some repassivation, while the substrate behaved actively.
watch_item: Residual porosity and incomplete interparticle bonding may still limit long-term corrosion durability despite improved passivation after polishing.
paper_title: Corrosion Behavior of Cold-Sprayed 316L Coatings: Effects of Deposition Temperature and Surface Condition
